quotes: The emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic has created an environment where many determinants of poor mental health are exacerbated. The need for up-to-date information on the mental health impacts of COVID-19 in a way that informs health system responses is imperative. quotes: This study, conducted as part of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2020, estimated the impact of the pandemic on the prevalence and burden of major depressive disorder and anxiety disorders across 204 countries and territories, stratified by age and sex. **Methods.** A systematic review identified population surveys reporting prevalence of depressive or anxiety disorders during the pandemic (January 2020 to January 2021). Eligible studies required a pre-pandemic baseline using the same instrument, location, and age group. From 5683 unique records, 48 studies met inclusion criteria (46 for major depressive disorder, 27 for anxiety disorders).

quotes: Prevalence surveys conducted during the pandemic could not be included without comparable pre-pandemic data (ie, using the same instrument, location, and age group) collected since 2013 to assess the change in prevalence. Longitudinal studies using samples representative of the general population were preferred, but cross-sectional studies were also included if comparable pre-pandemic prevalence data existed. Studies using random sampling were preferred; however, due to challenges imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic, there were few studies of this type. Studies using market research quota sampling were also included but were controlled for with a covariate in our analysis.

quotes: Case definitions for major depressive disorder and anxiety disorders followed DSM-IV-TR and ICD-10 criteria as applied in the GBD framework. The search covered sources published between January 1, 2020, and January 29, 2021, across PubMed, Google Scholar, the Eppi-centre COVID-19 living map, the DEPRESSD Project, the WHO COVID-19 literature database, COVID-Minds, MedRxiv, PsyArXiv, and grey literature, supplemented by expert consultation. No language restrictions were applied. Eligible studies reported prevalence of depressive or anxiety disorders during the pandemic and provided a comparable pre-pandemic baseline (same instrument, location, and age group) collected since 2013.

quotes: **Findings.** After adjustment for the pandemic, global major depressive disorder prevalence rose from 2470.5 per 100 000 (193 million people) to 3152.9 per 100 000 (246 million), yielding an additional 53.2 million cases—a 27.6% increase. Anxiety disorder prevalence rose from 3824.9 per 100 000 (298 million) to 4802.4 per 100 000 (374 million), adding 76.2 million cases—a 25.6% increase. Females experienced larger absolute and relative increases than males for both disorders. Younger age groups were affected more than older age groups. The pandemic imposed an additional 10.7 million DALYs for major depressive disorder and 9.05 million DALYs for anxiety disorders in 2020.
